title: OpenAI board member worries an AI "takeover" of society could be months away
author: Kyle Orland
body: How do you think you're going to die? If you go by the current statistics for deaths in the US , it's reasonable to expect that cancer or heart disease will eventually get you. But OpenAI Foundation board member and Alignment Research Center Executive Director Paul Cristiano thinks we should all be worried about another major mortality risk. Speaking at a lecture series this week , Cristiano bluntly told the audience in a Toronto Convention Center, "I think for most people in this room, the most likely reason they will die is because of an AI accident." In the opening lecture of a three-part series , Cristiano outlined his worries about the risk of an impending "AI takeover." He defined that as a situation where goal-pursuing AI systems "call the shots in the same sense that humans today call the shots and what happens on Earth" and where any human trying to stop them "would be as ineffective as if you or me was trying to stop the US military." Such a situation would likely lead to mass death and perhaps uninhabitable environments for humans, Cristiano said. Read full article Comments

title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
author: Dan Goodin
body: Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day. On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System. Turning a Windows defense against itself The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates. title: It's the end of the world as we know it, per a physicist's 1960 prediction
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: As of this morning, Microsoft is still scrambling to restore service following yesterday's global outage, with millions of users unable to access Outlook and other vital tools. It's not the end of the world, but it does seem fitting that this should happen on the day a physicist predicted would be the end of humanity: November 13, 2026. And it falls on a Friday, too. The physicist in question is Heinz von Foerster, who published a 1960 paper in the journal Science predicting that by today, overpopulation would reach the breaking point. It's not a new fear. English economist Thomas Malthus —one of the early pioneers in modeling population dynamics—made a similar prediction in 1798, claiming that a rapidly growing population would eventually exhaust the available food supply, and humanity would starve to death. His model rested on the assumption of exponential growth, but the equation is only applicable under specific conditions, such as scientists growing bacteria in a lab in a perfectly controlled environment. Even then, while growth occurs exponentially for a time, it does not continue forever. Population dynamics are notoriously tricky to calculate because there are so many variables to consider and so much unpredictability in the system. In his 1960 analysis, Von Foerster accurately measured past trends in population growth, but like Malthus, he assumed those trends would carry into the future largely unchanged. title: Scientists warn 1.5°C climate change threshold could arrive by 2029
author: Bob Berwyn, Inside Climate News
body: ANTALYA, Turkey—Amid upbeat green-tech pep talks and notices for happy hours at the annual United Nations COP31 climate change conference on Thursday, two new reports offered a stark reminder of how far the world remains from containing global warming. Climate Action Tracker , a nonprofit group that analyzes climate policies, found that the planet is still on track to warm nearly 5° Fahrenheit by 2100, a rise that would devastate coral reefs, disrupt agriculture and forests and melt most of the world’s ice. In a separate bulletin, the European Union’s Copernicus climate change service reported that global warming has accelerated significantly since the 2015 Paris climate agreement . When the Paris agreement was adopted, the average global temperature was projected to surpass the pact’s long-term threshold of 2.7° Fahrenheit above the preindustrial average around 2045. After another decade of global climate summits, warming is now projected to cross that benchmark as soon as 2029, according to Copernicus. Read full article Comments

title: Specialized’s Tarmac SL9 S-Level is built to wreck your Zone 2 ride
author: Eric Bangeman
body: I love a good Zone 2 ride . There’s nothing like getting on the bike, settling into a groove, and letting the miles (and hours) flow by. But sometimes when I hopped on the Specialized Tarmac SL9 S-Level, Zone 2 would turn into a tempo ride. It was like having a little imp—the stereotype dressed in red with the pitchfork—on my left shoulder whispering into my ear: “Go fast. This bike was built to go fast. Speed is good. You can do a Zone 2 ride tomorrow.” Normally, I'd count on the good imp—the dude with the harp and wings—on my right shoulder to restrain these urges. But the Tarmac is so seductive that he would just shrug and say “he’s got a point.” And in a moment of weakness, I would drop the hammer and head into the red, just because the SL9 makes that so rewarding. The Tarmac SL9 is Specialized’s aero road bike, with the S-Level sitting just below the S-Works in Specialized’s top tier of carbon, aero road bikes, where it replaced the Tarmac SL8 Pro. After it got an update this year, I spent several weeks riding it, putting nearly 1,000 miles on it Specialized offers the Tarmac SL9 in four models, all available with SRAM and Shimano drivetrains (Ars tested the SRAM version). Notably, you don't need to buy the top-of-the-line bike to get the top-of-the-line groupset. title: Watch SpaceXs wildest test yet: A 22-hour flight and a historic return
body: SpaceX will try to catch both halves of its giant Starship in one launch, grabbing the booster minutes after liftoff and the ship nearly a full day later. No one has pulled off such a feat before. If both attempts work, the company says it will become the first to recover an entire orbital rocket for reuse. SpaceX has caught its Super Heavy booster three times before, but it has never tried to catch the the ship the part that actually reaches orbit until now. This test, known as flight 15, seeks to make a leap in progress and could launch as soon as Friday, Nov. 13. Starship's flight 14 test was the first to enter orbit , but controllers cut its planned nine-hour mission short. This time, SpaceX wants the ship to stay in space for about 22 ½ hours and land both pieces back at its Starbase launch site in South Texas, where huge mechanical arms will be waiting to snatch them out of the air. The stakes reach far beyond Texas. NASA is counting on Starship as one of two lunar landers, along with Blue Origin's Blue Moon , to put astronauts on the moon as soon as 2028. To get there, Starship must refuel in orbit , which takes a series of fuel-hauling launches. SpaceX can only fly that often if it reuses its rockets the way airlines reuse jets. China, meanwhile, aims to land its own crew on the moon before 2030. And while SpaceX juggles the NASA contract, founder Elon Musk is laser-focused on his personal ambition of getting the rocket and ship ready to carry people to Mars and build a city there. title: 12 12 12 is the final boss of nonlinear TV
body: From multiple timelines to extended flashback episodes, you can barely get through a TV show nowadays without taking a hop, skip, and a jump through time. SEE ALSO: What's new to streaming this week? (Nov. 13, 2026) Of course, TV has a rich tradition of playing with chronology. Lost 's nonlinear approach revolutionized episodic storytelling, inspiring mystery-box series with several timelines like Westworld and Yellowjackets . Its use of character-focused flashbacks also lingers today, present everywhere from Paradise to Euphoria . While these techniques can build out fun puzzles or deepen our knowledge of characters, they can also devolve into nothing more than flashy gimmicks. Case in point: Apple TV's new heist drama 12 12 12 . Want more film and TV news and reviews delivered straight to your inbox? Sign up for Mashable s Top Stories newsletter or get Mashable push alerts today. 12 12 12 presents three timelines. Jamie Dornan as Paul and Jos Garcia as Serge in "12 12 12." Credit: Apple TV 12 12 12 unfolds across three different timelines: the 12 months of planning leading up to a billion-dollar heist on a Swiss bank; the 12 hours of the heist itself; and the 12 days after, in which FBI agent Jack Strickland (Anthony Mackie) hunts thief Paul Galvin (Jamie Dornan) and his accomplices. If you forget the structure of the show, don't worry. 12 12 12 lays it out for you at the top of every episode with the help of voiceover from Mackie. It also uses a series of split screens to remind you when we're entering a new timeline, be it "The Planning," "The Heist," or "The Takedown."

title: Boxed copies of GTA 6 are already out in the wild. Heres whats inside.
body: Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't launch until Nov. 19, but someone appears to have gotten their hands on a boxed PS5 copy more than a week early. The unboxing video , posted by GTA 6 Intel a fan account on X who claims to be "The largest GTA 6 fan community" racked up over 4 million views in 24 hours. It shows the person carefully opening the case to reveal a download code for the game and a folded, double-sided poster. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. title: Paper Tiger review: Adam Driver, Miles Teller, and Scarlett Johansson enter a tense love triangle
body: Marriage Story stars Adam Driver and Scarlett Johansson reunite in writer/director James Gray's Paper Tiger. But don't expect a desperate rehash of Noah Baumbach's divorce drama. For one thing, Gray is a filmmaker less drawn to such wall-punching theatrics, as evident through films like Two Lovers, Ad Astra, and Armageddon Time . For another, Driver and Johansson are not lovers in this film, though they are in a love triangle of sorts, with Miles Teller at the center. Gray gives Driver, Johansson, and Teller some unexpected roles, allowing each a place to display their range. But make no mistake, this is Driver's movie. What's Paper Tiger about? Set in 1986 New York City, Paper Tiger unfurls the story of a Jewish family from Queens that gets on the wrong side of the Russian mob. In a cozy home in Elmhurst, Irwin Pearl (Teller) raises his two sons, Benjamin (Roman Engel) and Scott (Gavin Goudey), with his dedicated housewife Linda (Johansson). Far from the cocky persona Teller forged through performances in The Spectacular Now, Whiplash , and the Divergent film series, the 39-year-old actor now oozes doofy dad energy. Teller's signature smirk is swapped for an aw-shucks smile, and a patronizing eyebrow raise that insists, "Father knows best." A pair of oversized eyeglasses completes the look; it's is such an evocative detail of the era that the title card reading "1986" might be deemed egregious. title: How to set up a joint AdultFriendFinder account
body: There's a fun feature of AdultFriendFinder that many users sleep on. The online hookup site actually allows couples to share an account . Registering as a couple, as opposed to a singleton (particularly a solo male ), helps boost your visibility on the site, since the search algorithms will treat your account as representing two people rather than one. That means it's easier for other users to find you in searches, helping you make more connections. The process of creating a joint account is reasonably straightforward, but there are some extra steps you'll need to take to ensure it is properly registered as a couple's account. Opens in a new window Credit: AdultFriendFinder AdultFriendFinder Learn More Here's a quick guide on everything you need to do. How to create a joint AFF account The first hurdle you'll have to pass is the "Who would you like to connect with?" screen, which offers up four options: Man, Woman, Couple, or Trans. This screen is totally inconsequential to creating a joint account, so if, for example, you're open to meeting people of all genders, don't worry that you've limited your options by your choice here. It doesn't matter overall. On the next screen, "Let's get your details," the site will prompt you to choose between a solo and a joint account. Under the "I am/we are a" tab, select "Couple." You'll then have to provide an answer to the "Your Orientation" screen before you can proceed. However, in 2019, he got more personal with Pain and Glory, a semi-autobiographical drama in which Antonio Banderas plays a thinly veiled version of the director as he looks back on his work and life, anxious to move forward with a new project. His latest, Bitter Christmas , serves as a sister film, echoing not only the semi-autobiographical element but also by casting a dashing actor in the role of an aging Almod var. However, Bitter Christmas gets self-reflexive as Ra l's story is interwoven with that in his screenplay. There, a once-revered art-house filmmaker named Elsa (B rbara Lennie) seeks to move away from directing commercials and return to screenwriting. Aside from their similar creative quest, both also have May-December romances with younger men, and both find inspiration for their new project in the tragedy that befalls a friend. In two layers, Almod var explores what it means to be an artist who may well cannibalize the stories of his loved ones for his art. title: Victorian Psycho review: What if Gothic horror were an eat-the-rich comedy?
body: Gothic horror is going from mad to madcap with Victorian Psycho, a horror comedy that follows a murderous governess to her next and possibly last appointment. Maika Monroe stars as Winifred Notty, a governess who is desperate to make a good impression on her new employers, the Pound family. The broad strokes of the plotline are tropes of Gothic horror. A seemingly fragile young woman must care for the young, defenseless children of a rich and twisted family. At night, strange noises might be heard about their grand house. The family's treasures go missing or are vandalized. Members of the staff vanish without a word. Could it be a ghost or ghoul whose very presence could drive this poor heroine mad? Well, no. Because from the very start, Victorian Psycho shows us its protagonist is already mad, and also the vicious thing that goes bump in the night. The title alone gives some clue of the topsy-turvy approach that Virginia Feito, who wrote the novel and this adapted screenplay, has to the genre. Director Zachary Wigon ( Sanctuary ) cements this cheeky attitude with an opening scene in which Winifred addresses the audience in voiceover while looking straight into the camera. There's a sense of Fleabag in this distorted direct address to the audience, as Winifred insists she is the sanest person she's ever met. This is just the first red flag, warning that Winifred Notty is much more than naughty. Soon after, a dismembered human ear tumbles out of her luggage; she regards it with slight irritation. title: In reversal, American Cancer Society urges routine prostate cancer screening
author: Beth Mole
body: In a significant update to its guidelines for prostate cancer screening, the American Cancer Society is now recommending that men get routinely screened for prostate cancer with a PSA test. Men at average risk should get a PSA test every two years from age 50 to 69, according to the new guidelines released Thursday. Men considered at high risk due to race and family history should start testing earlier, at 45, and most are recommended to get tested every year. Specifically, yearly testing starting at age 45 is recommended for all Black men, who have higher rates of prostate cancer. Non-Black men should also get yearly testing starting at 45 if a close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer before age 65, or if more than one of their relatives has had prostate cancer. On the other hand, if only one close relative was diagnosed with prostate cancer and it was diagnosed at age 65 or older, non-Black men in this case should start PSA screening at 45, but are recommended to get testing only every two years. title: How many billions are at stake if Jensen and Lori Huang divorce?
body: There are plenty of reasons Jensen Huang's resignation is a big deal. Not only does his departure leave Nvidia , the AI chipmaker he co-founded 33 years ago, looking for a new permanent CEO for the first time. It also puts the spotlight on the Huang family, whose ties to the company run well beyond its founder. To catch you up, Huang stepped down four days after first telling employees he'd been unfaithful to his wife of 41 years, Lori Huang. He made the admission after reports of a relationship with Alice Huang, a businesswoman, who first of all is unrelated to him, and whom U.S. intelligence officials suspect of spying for China. On Wednesday, the New York Times reported that he'd also had a relationship with Kimberly Powell, an Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. And then on Thursday, hours after resigning, Reuters reported that Huang had an "intimate relationship" with another Nvidia employee, whom the outlet did not name. To make matters worse (if possible), the Huangs' two children, Madison and Spencer, both work at Nvidia, making this whole scandal a family affair with a far more personal question at the center of it: What would happen to the Nvidia multi-billion dollar fortune if they divorced? Of course, this analysis doesn't mean the couple is divorcing Lori hasn t made any public comment. She and Jensen are deeply connected in business as co-trustees of three trusts that directly held nearly 669 million Nvidia shares in March. title: FAA expands AI advice to manage air traffic congestion across entire US airspace
author: Jeremy Hsu
body: The US government has expanded the use of an AI tool for advising air traffic controllers to assist in managing air traffic across the entire national airspace system. Airline executives have voiced support for the rollout, but the US labor union representing air traffic controllers has said it was not involved in designing or testing the AI-driven system. The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) says the $875 million SMART system has helped reroute 180 flights since being implemented in airspace over Washington, DC, on September 21. The agency claims that this saved an average of 10 minutes per flight and almost 80 gallons of fuel per flight—and it is apparently hoping such results can be replicated nationwide through the expanded deployment. “After a successful initial rollout to the National Capital Region in September, the FAA will now use SMART in the airspace of all 22 centers across the country to reduce delays, reduce fuel consumption and improve the travel experience for the flying public,” according to the agency statement posted on November 10. With Huang's resignation from the chipmaking giant that he helped found, who will take the helm at Nvidia? Let's take a look at some of the names. Colette Kress First up is Nvidia's longtime Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress , already a billionaire in her own right. And, if she's able to right the ship and help Nvidia come out of Huang's scandals relatively unscathed, she's a favorite to take the position long-term, too. Before being promoted to the interim CEO position, Kress has worked as the CFO at the company since 2013. She previously worked as CFO for divisions at Microsoft and Cisco. Nvidia's investors are familiar with her too from the company's quarterly earnings calls, so she may have the upper hand there too. title: What is Microsoft Exchange? The cloud tool behind Microsoft Outlook issues.
body: Microsoft's popular suite of enterprise products, known as Microsoft 365, which includes Outlook, Teams, and Copilot, suffered from a massive outage on Thursday. Or did it? While more than 100,000 users reported problems accessing Microsoft Outlook and Microsoft 365 on the platform DownDetector , Microsoft is saying it's actually a cloud tool called Microsoft Exchange that's causing problems. So, what is Microsoft Exchange ? And why does it being down affect your ability to access your email or message your coworkers? Microsoft Exchange is the backend cloud tool that sends data updates to Outlook. It's essentially the server that stores the actual data, handles the mail flow, syncs the data to services like Outlook, and controls account security policies. Put simply, Outlook is the front end; Exchange is the back end. For most users, though, this is a distinction without a difference. The end result is that users can't access their email, calendar, or messages. The company has been providing updates on the situation on X: This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Mashable reached out to Microsoft with questions about the outage, but the company has not responded, as of this writing.

title: Google rolls out Gemini 4 Hydrogen, finally replacing 3.8 Flash
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Google is continuing its elemental AI naming scheme with the new Gemini 4 Hydrogen . These names are less descriptive than the Pro/Flash monikers of earlier releases, but Hydrogen's purpose is clear: It replaces the faster, more economical Flash models most people in Google's ecosystem use. With Google's recent Argon and Carbon releases, the rollout was staged and began with cybersecurity researchers. Even when general availability began, Google restricted access to users paying for its most expensive AI subscription. The limits for Hydrogen are much more relaxed, with access beginning immediately. This model has replaced Gemini 3.8 Flash across the company's products. Google claims that Hydrogen represents a major improvement versus the previous Flash model. It runs in one of four thinking levels (low, medium, high, and the new xhigh), and even in high mode, it's 2.5 times faster than Flash 3.8. Plus, it reduces "fabricated claims" by more than 5x, according to Google's analysis. Users will also see gains in code generation, with Hydrogen more than tripling 3.8 Flash's score in Terminal-Bench. In some cases, Hydrogen even trades blows with Argon. It managed a score of 54 in the popular Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index with xhigh mode versus 50 for Argon. Read full article Comments

title: Netflix releases new trailer for Ray Gunn
author: Jennifer Ouellette
body: We caught the first trailer for the upcoming Netflix animated film Ray Gunn in September and were charmed by director Brad Bird's blend of a Jetsons-like future with classic 1930s noir detective thrillers. Bird has described it as a mashup of The Maltese Falcon and Buck Rogers , and the latest trailer definitely gives off that energy. As previously reported , Bird has directed some of our all-time favorite animated films: The Iron Giant (1999), The Incredibles (2004), and Ratatouille (2007), with the latter two snagging well-deserved Oscar wins. He's been kicking around the idea for Ray Gunn for the last 30 years, working on his many other film projects while the Ray Gunn script—co-written by Matthew Robbins, who also co-wrote 1987’s Batteries Not Included with Bird—“stayed in a filing cabinet at Warner Brothers,” the director said earlier this year. The film’s inspiration came when Bird heard the opening of the B-52s’ “ Planet Claire ” (a personal favorite that also provides the soundtrack to the new trailer) and initially thought it was a cover of Henry Mancini’s theme music from the classic TV show Peter Gunn . Bird is a longtime fan of film noir and hard-boiled detectives, and he came up with the idea of a futuristic detective named Ray Gunn (a play on " raygun ," of course). “It’s film noir and a hard-boiled detective story, but it’s got a lot more comedy and a lot more action than the average film noir,” said Bird . title: Man's secret use of synthetic testosterone for cows nearly destroyed his heart
author: Beth Mole
body: For 11 years, a Massachusetts man had an alarming array of health problems, most notably that his heart kept failing. He landed in the hospital over and over again, needed life support at one point, spent years going to specialists, and underwent a barrage of tests along the way. But through it all, he never revealed a key detail behind his ailments: He was taking powerful, illicit synthetic testosterone derivatives (aka anabolic-androgenic steroids, or AAS). One of the drugs he took was approved only for use in animals; it's primarily used to beef up cows. Left in the dark, his doctors had to puzzle this out on their own. In a case report in this week's issue of the New England Journal of Medicine, they explain how they did it. They also offer a warning: These cases will only become more common, and clinicians need to know what they look like. Read full article Comments

Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies in the world, with a nearly $4 trillion valuation , and Huang was the company's original CEO and co-founder. The company's board of directors shared a CEO transition plan on its website, saying Huang has also resigned as president and as a member of the board, effective immediately. The company's CFO, Colette Kress, will serve as interim CEO, while also maintaining her CFO responsibilities. The board has begun searching for a new CEO, looking both inside and outside the company. The tech industry has been closely watching Nvidia and its stock ever since news first broke by the New York Times that Huang had not one, but two affairs, including one with an accused Chinese spy. title: Apple says it will shut down its Apple Support Community forums after 28 years
body: If you've ever had a problem with your MacBook , iPhone , or Apple account, a quick Google search for a fix likely sent you to a relevant thread on the Apple Support Community at discussions.apple.com , where Apple customers tried to help their fellow Apple fans out. That won't be the case anymore. On Tuesday, Apple announced that it would be closing down the Apple Support Community, the official forum for Apple customers looking for help from other Apple users with their Apple products. Apple disabled posting in the Apple Support Community on Tuesday. The platform is still viewable in a read-only state. However, the forums will be shuttered for good on Nov. 20. A prompt now appears at the top of the Apple Support Community website and all of its posts with Apple's announcement of the forum's closure: "The Apple Support Community will permanently close on November 20, 2026. Starting today, the site will no longer accept new posts and is available in a read-only state. You can continue to find trusted guidance and support on the official Apple Support site. We want to thank the community members who have contributed their time and expertise to help others with their Apple products." Anyone who has ever had an Apple product likely found themselves on the Apple Support Community at some point . Even if they didn't sign up to ask a question themselves, the answer to their question likely existed in the Apple Support Community archives, helping numerous customers avoid reaching out directly to Apple's official support. title: The amazing disappearing exoplanet
author: John Timmer
body: One nice thing about discovering exoplanets is that, once you work out how long their orbits take, they continue to show up like clockwork. The timing is so regular, in fact, that we can use variations to detect the gravitational influence of additional planets in the same exosolar system. And the precise timing is useful in that we can rely on it to point telescopes at the system when we know some of the light we detect has passed through the planet's atmosphere. Except when we can't. On Monday, researchers reported on an exoplanet that simply stopped showing up. TOI-2535b is a hot Jupiter-sized planet we've been observing as it transits between its host star, TOI-2535, and Earth for about seven years now. But it recently stopped showing up, and researchers suspect that's due to an unseen companion orbiting in a different plane. Read full article Comments

title: Jensen Huang resigns: A timeline of the Nvidia affair
body: The AI boom has put chatbots at work, AI-generated videos in our feeds, and data centers on the agenda at town halls. Nvidia , a company that got its start making computer games look better, now supplies the chips that power much of the AI industry . That made Nvidia one of the world's most valuable companies and its chips some of the most sought-after technology in the world. And on Thursday, Nov. 12, the company announced that it had lost the only CEO it had ever had. The story goes back more than a year and reads a little like an HBO drama, with alleged spies, extramarital affairs, and corporate intrigue. Let's break down the timeline of the Jensen Huang resignation based on what came to light and when. SEE ALSO: Nvidia live updates: Jensen Huang is out as CEO Oct. 9, 2025 A chip-export investigation puts Megaspeed in the spotlight Last year, the New York Times reported that U.S. officials were looking into whether Nvidia chips meant for data centers in Southeast Asia had ended up in China. The chips in question had been bought by Megaspeed, a Singapore company that rented out computing power. U.S. export rules limit China's access to some of Nvidia s most advanced AI hardware, to protect Nvidia's trade secrets and the United States' competitive edge over China in the AI arms race. Singapore police were also looking into whether Megaspeed had broken local laws, but at the time, Nvidia said it had no reason to believe the chips had been sent elsewhere. title: Nvidia stock plunges as CEO Jensen Huang resigns: How low it might go
body: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has just resigned from the company he co-founded amid reports of two alleged affairs, including one with a woman that U.S. intelligence believes is a Chinese spy, according to a bombshell New York Times report . Thanks to the AI boom, Nvidia has become one of the most valuable companies in the world. And, as a result, Huang had seemingly become the de facto head of the AI industry. Huang's resignation will not only send reverberations through the tech world, but the broader global economy as well. As one could assume, Wall Street didn't take the news well. As of Thursday morning, Nvidia stock had plunged on the news of the affairs and rumors about a possible resignation from Huang. So far, the stock has struggled to rebound after Nvidia's board of directors announced the official CEO transition . Nvidia stock hit as low as $152 per share when the stock market opened. It's currently trading around $162 per share as of publication time, showing some recovery now that the resignation is official. Nvidia's Wall Street woes began on Nov. 8 when Jensen Huang confirmed the reports that he had been having an affair. Outlets including the New York Times and Financial Times identified the woman involved as Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at a Singapore-based company, Megaspeed. U.S. intelligence strongly believes that Huang has been working with China's top intelligence agency as a spy, according to the Times. title: Google pushes privacy angle as Gemini-powered smartglasses debut starting at $395
author: Ryan Whitwam
body: Smartglasses have always faced an uphill road to acceptance. Not only is propping a computer up on your nose an uncomfortable proposition, but the privacy aspect has been vexing people since the Google Glass days . Now, Google is ready to take another swing at " intelligent eyewear " for the Gemini era after previewing its plans a couple of times. The first glasses are up for preorder today from Gentle Monster and Warby Parker, but they're no impulse buy. These devices are a collaboration between Google, Samsung, and the aforementioned eyewear designers. Gentle Monster and Warby Parker have each designed a few different frames, with options for transparent and tinted lenses. Samsung is providing the computing hardware that fits inside them, and Google has the software covered. Warby Parker has designed three frames for Google eyewear, called Alden, Reid, and Wren (see above). They are available with both standard optical and sun lenses in Pine, Saddle, and Jet Black colors at $395 and higher. Warby Parker is only selling devices in the US. Gentle Monster has gone a bit further with six styles, but Google hasn't told us any names for those yet. They come in dark red, pink, gray, and yellow colors and are available with clear, tinted, blue, or brown lenses. The Gentle Monster styles start a little higher at $449, and they will be available in the US and South Korea. Read full article Comments

title: Jensen Huang officially resigns as Nvidia CEO
body: For the first time in its 33-year history, Nvidia has a new CEO. Jensen Huang, who co-founded the chipmaker in 1993 and led it through the AI boom, resigned Thursday. He also stepped down as president and gave up his seat on the board, effective immediately. Nvidia gave no reason for his departure, though we can think of a few ( namely, two ). SEE ALSO: Jensen Huang Nvidia affair scandal: What we know, what we don t For now, the job will go to CFO of Nvidia, Colette Kress, who has run Nvidia's finances since 2013. She'll stay on as chief financial officer while serving as interim CEO, and the board will look both inside and outside the company for a permanent replacement. The board also picked longtime director Harvey C. Jones to serve as its first chair. The announcement came a day after Nvidia's board met to discuss Huang's future. Why? Earlier Nov. 11, the Times reported that Huang had an affair with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia's vice president of healthcare and one of his direct reports. Though that wasn't the only affair. On Sunday, Huang told employees he had been "unfaithful to my wife" without naming the person involved...but the New York Times identified her as Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed, whom U.S. intelligence officials reportedly suspected of spying for China. China denied the allegations, and Nvidia's board, and Donald Trump, said that it had no reason to believe U.S. national security or company secrets had been compromised. body: The Cybertruck saga continues. Days after Tesla CEO Elon Musk said the company would wind down production of its electric pickup , he's backtracking that decision, but not by much. Last week, Musk said Tesla will stop producing Cybertrucks at Gigafactory Texas "around the middle of next year." Given that it's the only factory where Cybertrucks are manufactured, that meant the end of the road for the Cybertruck, with the company using the production capacity for its autonomous taxi car, the Cybercab . Musk quickly followed up by saying that the demand for Cybertruck is strong and that the order rate "far exceeds" the company's production rate. "We will try to make as many as possible before shutting down the line in about 8 months," he wrote on X. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. Counting from the day he said it (early November 2026), that would mean ending production in early June 2027. Now, however, Musk says Tesla will extend that deadline by a couple of months. This Tweet is currently unavailable. It might be loading or has been removed. "In order to work through more of the Cybertruck order backlog, production will be extended through the end of summer 2027," he wrote on X. "This is not the smartest move from a profit-maximizing standpoint btw, but there must be some room in this world for sentimentality or what s the point," he added . Donny bone spurs and his sidekick Elon cut thousands of veteran jobs last year. 28,000 of those jobs were at the VA , including thousands of nurses, psychologists, and social workers. body: Still reeling from the blue wave post-midterms , Donald Trump 's media appearances lately have been somewhat subdued. It's a through-line Seth Meyers picked up on during Late Night on Wednesday, from the president's viral 60 Minutes appearance to his real-time reaction to the election results calling into Fox News . "The sadder Trump gets, the more emboldened the press gets," said Meyers. "In fact, there's one clip from a few days ago that really sums up the mood at the White House right now." That clip? Sky News international affairs editor Dominic Waghorn asking Trump , "How does it feel being a loser, Mr. President?" Choosing not to answer, the president can be seen walking quickly away from the group of reporters outside the White House. "Damn, he was out of there so fast, I thought he was gonna Mary Poppins out of frame," reacted Meyers. "It's so funny to get asked what does it feel like to be a loser and then walk away alone in the rain. How does it feel to be a loser? I'll take my answer non-verbally. While it's unclear whether this affair is still ongoing, multiple sources speaking to the Times stated that Huang and Powell were seen being affectionate with each other as recently as this March. Huang has been married to his wife since 1985, while Powell is reportedly married as well. Meanwhile, Nvidia s board is allegedly looking to oust Huang. The company had previously stated that Huang would stay on as CEO during the investigation into his affair with Megaspeed executive Alice Huang (no relation). However, the revelation of his relationship with Powell may have changed that plan. The Wall Street Journal reports that the board now intends to remove Huang. Reuters reported that the board was meeting late Wednesday to decide his future. title: GTA 6 preorders top $1 billion as Hollywood eyes record launch weekend
body: It's been 13 years since Rockstar dropped a new mainline Grand Theft Auto , so there was always going to be a fairly large crowd for the next one. A week before launch, we're getting a sense of just how big that crowd is. Eight days before its Nov. 19 release, GTA 6 has already topped $1 billion in preorders, according to an estimate from market research firm Sensor Tower . The firm also estimates that players worldwide have preordered more than 10 million digital copies for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S . (About three out of every four orders were for PS5, The Washington Post reported on Nov. 11.) The previous game, GTA V , hit that same $1 billion milestone three days after it went on sale in 2013, according to publisher Take-Two Interactive . Take-Two has yet to share its own preorder tally for the sequel, though CEO Strauss Zelnick wrote in a release on Monday that orders were reaching "unprecedented levels. " Both Sony and Microsoft also said it's already the most preordered game in the history of their respective digital stores. Rockstar opened preloads on Nov. 10 , so players can get the download out of the way before launch day. The hype for GTA 6 has been building for nearly three years, ever since Rockstar released its first trailer in December 2023 . It drew more than 90 million YouTube views in 24 hours, setting a Guinness World Record , and has 302 million views as of Nov. 11, 2026. title: T-Mobile illegally imposed 50GB cap on low-income home Internet plan, NY says
author: Jon Brodkin
body: T-Mobile violated a New York state law by imposing a 50GB-per-month data cap and reducing speeds to less than a megabit per second on home Internet plans it is required to offer people with low incomes, New York government officials alleged. T-Mobile agreed to a settlement requiring it to scrap the data and speed limits, to offer the required low-income plans to more parts of the state, and to make it easier for customers to find information about the plans. The settlement requires T-Mobile to eliminate the speed limits and expand availability of the plans within 120 days. The alleged legal violation and the settlement are related to T-Mobile's wireless home Internet service, not the company's mobile plans. Governor Kathy Hochul and New York Attorney General Letitia James announced the settlement on Monday, saying that a state investigation found T-Mobile violated the New York Affordable Broadband Act (ABA). Anduril reported on the success of the tech demo mission Tuesday. title: Disney parks launches new app to get you off apps
body: Going to a Disney park is supposed to transport you somewhere magical, but for many, the experience requires a very rote part of modern life: staring at your phone. Disney has separate apps for its resorts in California and Florida, as well as those in France, Japan, and China. Booking Lightning Lane appointments (an extra charge that lets guests jump long lines for rides), nabbing meal reservations, and ordering mobile food items all require checking times on the app. It s something that Disney guests have to do often if they don t want to wait hours for Space Mountain or a meal at the Blue Bayou restaurant. Disney brass even acknowledged that its tech-forward approach has lessened the park experience, with Walt Disney Imagineering President Bruce Vaughn saying last year that reliance on the various apps "breaks the spell" of visiting a Disney resort. Disney s first experiment to reduce phone use at its parks was revealed this week. The company just launched the Disney Imagineering Labs app (yes, a new app to reduce smartphone use). The first offering of the app is now available to select Magic Key participants (annual passholders) Secrets of the Spire in Star Wars: Galaxy s Edge. Described by the Disney Tourist blog as an interactive game within the parks' Star Wars: Galaxy s Edge section, the app offers minigames and challenges. It s not very clear how this reduces phone usage while at the park, though. body: The Trump administration’s fight to stop suspected leaks of top-secret military information on LinkedIn can’t sweep in “a vast number of confidential sources” of random journalists “who have no conceivable relationship” to the Department of Justice’s investigation, an appeals court ruled Tuesday. The order came after the DOJ asked LinkedIn to turn over 18 months of communications from targeted journalists who collectively published more than 1,000 articles on many different topics over that time period. The request was not limited to journalists involved in a controversial report from a news outlet that Trump said exposed confidential military information in a foreign country. (The outlet is not being named to protect national security secrets.) Instead, the DOJ cast a wide net, requesting extensive LinkedIn data on journalists who had any possible link to the journalists around the time the report was drafted. The majority of journalists have LinkedIn accounts and publish their contact information to encourage sources to connect on the platform, LinkedIn argued. So allowing that government overreach went beyond harming targeted journalists and threatened to undermine a critical platform where journalists frequently connect with confidential sources, judges ruled. Even more concerning, the Trump administration secured a secrecy order barring LinkedIn from telling anyone about the sweeping request for a year. That left journalists unaware for far too long that their First Amendment rights had been compromised, judges ruled. Read full article Comments

title: Big Walk used AI to fix a bug. Now the indie gaming world is having a reckoning.
author: Kyle Orland
body: The last few years have seen significant debate over the widespread use of AI-powered tools in game development and the responsible disclosure of that usage to players. That debate has exploded into a full-blown controversy in the indie game development space this week, as Big Walk developer House House has publicly and belatedly disclosed minimal AI use in its popular co-operative puzzle exploration game. This particular controversy has been brewing behind the scenes for months, as judges and jury members for the prestigious Independent Games Festival Awards discussed the issue in private discussion groups. But the debate started to break into public view on Monday when 19 members of the 50-plus-member jury released a signed statement outlining a stance "declining to vote for any game that uses generative AI in any capacity." Noting "a significant increase in the number of submitted games developer with generative AI tools," the group of jurors called out AI's ecological, economic, psychological, and labor harms in rejecting tools whose use, they said, is still "not a foregone conclusion in our industry." title: Firefox’s free built-in VPN has no data cap through January 2027
body: Going home for the holidays? Or simply traveling for Thanksgiving, Christmas, or New Year's? Firefox and its built-in VPN has your privacy covered at not cost to you. Mozilla , the organization behind the Firefox web browser , has announced that it will be providing free unlimited data for its built-in VPN to all of its users from Nov. 10, 2026 through Jan. 31, 2027. That's now up until the end of January. Firefox advertises its VPN first and foremost as a privacy feature. A VPN hides a user's real IP address, thus masking exactly what location that user is browsing from. For example, Firefox says its VPN will help hide the sites you visit from shared WiFi networks in public spaces or at a relative's home. However, Firefox knows that many VPN users also utilize the feature to change their location in order to access region-locked websites and platforms. And, according to its announcement, Firefox is cool with that too. How to try the Firefox VPN Firefox's free built-in VPN is available for Firefox on both desktop and Android. Mozilla says the feature is coming to iOS devices soon too. In order to take advantage of Firefox's offer of unlimited data use via their VPN, simply sign up for a Mozilla account . Then, in the Firefox web browser, select the VPN icon in the toolbar on desktop. On Android, tap on the three-dot menu and select Settings followed by VPN. From there, follow the setup process and turn the VPN on. Mozilla explicitly reminded users in its announcement that VPNs do not make users anonymous or hide on-device browsing history. title: Scarlet Witchs return is everything thats wrong with the MCU
body: The biggest story out of VisionQuest 's finale wasn't the long-awaited reunion between twins Tommy and Billy Maximoff (Ruaridh Mollica and Joe Locke). Nor was it Vision (Paul Bettany) and Ultron's (James Spader) touching heart-to-heart about grief. Instead, it was the resurrection of Wanda Maximoff (Elizabeth Olsen) at the hands of Dr. Doom (Robert Downey Jr.), which occurs during the second of VisionQuest 's two mid-credits scenes . SEE ALSO: 'VisionQuest' could have done anything, and it just did this In theory, the return of Scarlet Witch is an exciting one, as she's one of the most powerful heroes in the MCU. Now that she's apparently under Dr. Doom's thrall, that will spell major trouble for the Avengers in Avengers: Doomsday . Powers aside, Wanda is also one of the MCU's most compelling characters, with Olsen's grief-stricken turn in WandaVision earning her an Emmy nomination. Yet the reality of Wanda's return is that it, like much of the MCU post- Avengers: Endgame , is downright exhausting. Wanda's return is proof that the MCU has no stakes anymore. Wanda is the latest MCU mainstay to return from the dead. In addition to the return of everyone who got blipped by Thanos, characters like Loki (Tom Hiddleston) and Gamora (Zoe Salda a) both stuck around after their deaths in Avengers: Infinity War thanks to some timeline meddling. The changes greatly expand the scope of its next-generation Nighthawk general-use processors by adding a version with over 500 programmable qubits. At the same time, it's stepping back a bit on its plan to link multiple Nighthawk processors together, dropping the intended number of linked systems from nine to two. title: Logitech offers employees a day off to play GTA 6 at launch
body: Grand Theft Auto VI is tantalizingly close, so for many people, it's probably too late to submit a PTO request for its Nov. 19 release date. Not for Logitech employees, though. The PC accessory maker announced that its employees would be given the option to take time off for new video game releases, according to IGN . Logitech's announcement was almost certainly timed for the release of GTA 6 (there are basically no other major upcoming releases this year, for obvious reasons). However, the new "Logi Game Day" perk will seemingly apply to more games than just Rockstar's latest open-world crime adventure. SEE ALSO: 'GTA 6' preorders are live: Where to buy for PS5 and Xbox Logitech cited an internal study which found that 81 percent of video game enjoyers "believe that gaming builds real-world confidence, reduces anxiety, and correlates with stronger day-to-day work performance." Whether or not that's actually true, Logitech is buying into the idea, enabling its employees to play hooky for gaming purposes. "It s time to retire the stereotype that gaming is a waste of time," Logitech CEO Hanneke Faber said, according to IGN. "As a company designing products for work and play, we see every day how engagement in one sphere supports performance in the other." body: If all the emails flooding your inbox weren't enough of an indication, we're closing in on the biggest shopping holiday of the year. Black Friday technically doesn't happen until the dishes from Thanksgiving are scrubbed and put away. But retailers have gotten antsy over the years, kicking off their sales days or weeks in advance. Heck, the whole month of November is basically Black Friday at this point. If you're hoping to do some discount shopping this holiday season, knowing precisely when to shop each major retailer's official Black Friday sale is key. To help you best strategize this season, we've rounded up the essential dates and times below. When is Black Friday 2026? Black Friday always lands on the day after Thanksgiving and the fourth Friday in November. In 2026, that happens to be on Friday, Nov. 27. As you've probably noticed, however, most major retailers began rolling out early Black Friday deals as soon as the calendar switched to November. Likewise, some will draw things out even longer with Black Friday discounts that last far past the official shopping holiday. Black Friday is no longer a single 24-hour extravaganza; it's a full season. SEE ALSO: Amazon Prime Day vs. Black Friday: When are the deals better? Cyber Monday , the more online-centric shopping holiday, falls on the Monday after Black Friday. In 2026, that's on Monday, Nov. 30. Most retailers shift into Cyber Monday mode by the Saturday after Black Friday. It's silly, really, but the lines between the two deal-shopping holidays have been blurred beyond recognition. title: Trump wanted little Kei trucks for America, Toyota makes it happen
author: Jonathan M. Gitlin
body: The idea that Americans should be offered a greater choice of smaller cars has support from strange bedfellows indeed. After all, who could forget President Trump—usually one to take a maximalist approach to any problem— announcing last year that he wanted the Department of Transportation to make Japan’s diminutive “Kei” cars legal here in the US. Ars’ attempts to get DoT to tell us more about the potential influx of little vehicles have mostly fallen on deaf ears. But this week, there has been movement on the topic, with Toyota announcing that it will bring back the Scion brand with the KEI-01. What’s a Kei car? Here in the US, the preponderance of humongous SUVs is a consequence largely of government policies, specifically corporate average fuel economy standards that made it less profitable to sell smaller, efficient cars. Japan’s Kei cars are what happens if the government instead restricts the size, engine capacity, and power output. Read full article Comments

title: Google DeepMind just mathematically verified key parts of Signal
author: Lily Hay Newman, wired.com
body: Google DeepMind researchers used agentic AI to mathematically prove, or “formally verify,” a number of the Signal protocol’s key cryptographic guarantees—a landmark development for the widely used cryptography and AI itself. Conducted as a sort of proof-of-concept project in just four weeks, the work is significant in two ways. It serves as further independent validation of the cryptography that protects massive quantities of the world's communications on platforms like the Signal app , Google Messages, and WhatsApp. And it demonstrates Google DeepMind's formal verification capabilities using a new AI framework called AlphaProof Code. More broadly, AI-aided formal verification is having a moment, but it is unclear how practical it will be for widespread use and how effective it can be at securing large amounts of code. Proponents of formal verification have long referred to it as a sort of holy grail in software security, because it uses math to check and validate that software is functioning as intended—in other words, that it doesn't have critical vulnerabilities. title: How to Rob a Bank review: This eat-the-rich thriller from Amazon has the psychological depth of a kiddie pool
body: Earlier this year, I reflected in my review of How to Make A Killing that cinema has been riding a wave of eat-the-rich comedies since 2019, when Parasite and Ready or Not made class conflict into ghoulish fun. Since then, we've seen the good ( Triangle of Sadness , The Menu , Send Help , I Love Boosters ), the bad ( How to Make a Killing ), and the truly awful ( The Running Man reboot). So, how does How to Rob a Bank, the latest from David Leitch, stack up? Oh, very poorly, and that's actually shocking at first glance. SEE ALSO: 'Triangle of Sadness' review: The "eat the rich" comedy goes gross-out, and it's great Let's consider the talent behind How to Rob a Bank . For starters, the production is helmed by David Leitch, who's directed such compelling action movies as Atomic Blonde , Deadpool 2, and The Fall Guy. The original screenplay comes from Mark Bianculli, a writer who worked on Hunters , an intense drama about a group that hunts down Nazis. The ensemble cast boasts Nicholas Hoult, Anna Sawai, John C. Reilly, Zo Kravitz, and Pete Davidson. All this suggests that a bank robbery thriller centered on class warfare might feature explosive action, challenging ideas, and rich emotional moments. However, produced and distributed by billionaire Jeff Bezos' Amazon MGM Studios, this eat-the-rich movie never dares to get that deep. Instead, How to Rob a Bank is a flashy, brainless mockery of the great American bank robbery movie. Who could guess why? How to Rob a Bank dabbles in class politics. title: Moon phase today: What the Moon will look like on November 11, 2026
body: The Moon is now a little further into its Waxing Crescent phase, with a small amount of its surface illuminated by the Sun. It should be slightly easier to spot tonight, although there's still not much to see in the way of lunar features. What is today's Moon phase? As of Wednesday, Nov. 11, the NASA's Daily Moon Guide tracker tells us the Moon is in the Waxing Crescent phase, with 4% of its surface visible. When is the next Full Moon? The next Full Moon will take place on November 24. What are Moon phases? The Moon takes approximately 29.5 days to complete one full cycle. As it orbits Earth, the amount of sunlight reflecting off its surface that we can see changes, creating the different phases. This takes us from the New Moon to the Full Moon and back again, before the cycle begins once more, according to NASA . The eight phases are: New Moon - The Moon is between Earth and the sun, so the side we see is dark (in other words, it's invisible to the eye). Waxing Crescent - A small sliver of light appears on the right side (Northern Hemisphere). First Quarter - Half of the Moon is lit on the right side. It looks like a half-Moon. Waxing Gibbous - More than half is lit up, but it's not quite full yet. Full Moon - The whole face of the Moon is illuminated and fully visible. Waning Gibbous - The Moon starts losing light on the right side. (Northern Hemisphere) Third Quarter (or Last Quarter) - Another half-Moon, but now the left side is lit. Waning Crescent - A thin sliver of light remains on the left side before going dark again.

Sauron (Charlie Vickers) is comfortably in control of most of Middle-earth, and he's got a whole host of allies to help him keep a firm grip on the world. Think of The Rings of Power 's Nazgnag l as the first step in that transformation. They've already got the black cloaks down. Next up? Corruption and an eternal life of undead servitude. Fun! body: Like the synthezoid at its center, Marvel's VisionQuest contains multitudes. It's a genre-bending adventure, a reflection on flawed father-son dynamics, and an ambitious attempt to tie up the loose ends of the so-called WandaVision trilogy. title: Seagate's new hybrid drive raises some old questions
author: Nick Indge
body: Seagate doesn't think hybrid drives are done just yet. On Tuesday, the company announced the launch of the new FireCuda Forge line of storage drives. The new drives combine the high capacity of a traditional plattered HDD with the speed and responsiveness of a user-supplied solid-state drive (SSD). The new hybrid storage solution is Seagate's first to be powered and managed by the new Alkemi intelligent storage platform. The FireCuda Forge is available right now through Seagate's web store , and comes in 8TB ($699) or 20TB ($899) HDD configurations—neither of which includes the required SSD. Users will have to bring their own SSD, with some specific restrictions. The FireCuda Forge is compatible with M.2 2280 NVMe drives that are PCIe Gen3 or higher. The maximum supported NVMe capacity is 1TB, which means that's as much data as you'll be able to dedicate to storage on the "fast side" of the hybrid setup. The NVMe will require minimum speeds of 2,400MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write, and a unit with DRAM cache is recommended. Seagate claims 2,500MB/s read and 2,000MB/s write speeds for the combined system, along with USB4 and support for Windows 11 and macOS 26+. Credit: Seagate Read full article Comments

title: The US military seems to be getting nervous about the launch supply crunch
author: Stephen Clark
body: The US military is taking a new approach to prop up commercial launch companies as SpaceX looks to wind down its Falcon rocket program, suggesting defense officials see the workhorse rocket's retirement as a potential national security risk. The Pentagon's Office of Strategic Capital has twice in the last two weeks announced it was sending cash to two of SpaceX's competitors in the launch business. First, on October 26, the office announced a $150 million conditional loan commitment to Stoke Space. Military officials revealed a second $150 million Pentagon loan Tuesday for Rocket Lab. Stoke Space and Rocket Lab are the first two launch companies to receive significant support from the Office of Strategic Capital (OSC), an organization established in 2022 to infuse companies developing "vital" national security technologies with capital. OSC has been on a loan spree in recent weeks, committing hundreds of millions of dollars to companies specializing in batteries, drones, and semiconductors.
